- When sentiment is consistently negative over recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast upward slightly to avoid underestimating rebound.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior peak), model often overshoots and fails to account for subsequent mean reversion; reduce forecast peak by 5–10% and add a slight downward slope after the spike.
- If sentiment flips from negative to positive mid-period, model often lags in recognizing the shift; increase forecast sensitivity to sentiment change and adjust early in the horizon.
- Model frequently underestimates late-period (last 5–7 days) price movements, especially when sentiment turns positive; apply a 2–3% upward bias to final 5–7 days if sentiment is positive.
- When sentiment is mixed or neutral, model tends to average out, missing volatility; use sentiment-weighted smoothing: higher weight to recent sentiment if >50% positive or negative.
